messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — elevated p99 latency on /v1/chat/completions (eu-west-1) for model=mistral-1-large. p99=2.8s, p95=540ms over last 5m — automated effort: start
vika: ack. i'm on it. looking at route-level splits and recent deploys
alex: rolling deploy? i didn't push anything to serving last hour
sam: ops: seeing a spike in tail latency specifically for routes with long-context prompts (>2048)
vika: grabbing logs and trace. can someone check routing percentage for fallback models
oncall: handing off to vika — i need to run to a meeting, ping back in 15 if still paged
vika: found a hot route: /v1/chat/completions?system_prompt=... backpressure on kv-cache eviction. QPS for that route jumped 3x from one customer
olivia: customer-impact check: only 2 customers in eu-west hit the long-prompts pattern, but both are high-traffic. they're seeing timeouts
mike: mitigation idea: temporarily split routing so long-context requests go to a slower-but-dedicated pool; short ones to the fast pool. Can we change routing policy without deploy?
alex: we have dynamic routing policy flags. can flip a route tag with:
```bash
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/route/modify -d '{\'route\':\'/v1/chat/completions\', \'tag\': \'long-context:downgrade\'}'
```
vika: doing that now. also increasing KV cache size for that pool by +20% as a quick fix
incident-bot: action: route-tag update applied by vika at 1942001248
vika: monitoring — p99 dropped from 2.8s -> 1.6s in 2m after route split
sam: nice. should we also suppress noisy alerts while this stabilizes? current p99 alert is firing per-route at 1s, causing repeat pages
olivia: agree. customers are affected but mitigation in progress. suggest squelching p99 pager for routes with QPS < 10 and instead surface to ops channel
mike: propose new temporary alert rule:
```yaml
alert: HighChatCompletionsP99
expr: (
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le,route,model) (rate(http_request_latency_seconds_bucket{path=\'/v1/chat/completions\'}[5m])))
) > 1.0
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: page
  route: '{{ $labels.route }}'
annotations:
  summary: 'p99 latency > 1.0s for route {{ $labels.route }}'
```
and add a condition: if route_qps < 10 then severity=warning (no page)
alex: we can implement route_qps check with an extra query `avg(rate(http_requests_total{path='/v1/chat/completions'}[5m])) by (route)`
vika: i've applied a squelch for low-volume routes (`qps < 8`) and bumped the p99 page window to 10m to reduce noise
olivia: please note for postmortem: don't widen alert threshold globally — we need per-model/per-route baselining
sam: agreed. also need a new dashboard panel: per-model p95/p99, route QPS, % routed to fallback pool, cache hit ratio. I'll make a grafana panel and link it
vika: created temporary dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/abcd/chat-completions-surge — added panels for model=mistral-1-large, route split %, cache evictions
mike: customer update: told both customers we have a mitigation and are monitoring. no SLA breaches yet but risk remains
oncall: handoff: i'll pick up in 2h if still noisy. vika to own until then
vika: post-incident actions:
- document routing flipbook and emergency knobs
- add per-model p95/p99 baselines to alert automation
- add squelch rule: per-route QPS threshold for paging
- add regression alert if cache eviction rate spikes > 2x
alex: also add a runbook step to prefer routing to dedicated pool rather than rolling back model version (rollback can cause other issues)
olivia: will own customer comms and add notes to incident ticket
incident-bot: incident acknowledged closed->monitoring at 1942003420 (status: mitigated, watch period 2h)
vika: thanks all. filing follow-up ticket: INF-7892 — alert tuning and dashboard work
sam: assigning INF-7892 to eng-sre and eng-runtime, due EOD next week
mike: :thumbsup: 
vika: logging end of thread. if p99 creeps back up, re-open pager
